mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (as of the most recent month) is associated with higher S&P 500 forward 20-day returns, reflecting the inverse relationship between short-term interest rates and equity valuations due to reduced discount rates on future cash flows.
failure_condition: Rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day forward returns is less than 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over the past month indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes economic slowdowns and negative equity returns due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings pressure.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 5.0% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises above 5.0% in the past month, or the Rank IC is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rapidly rising inflation (CPIAUCSL increase >0.5% in the past month) and persistently low interest rates (FEDFUNDS <0.7%) signals an imminent aggressive monetary tightening, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns due to heightened recession fears and equity repricing.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises >0.5% in past month AND FEDFUNDS <0.7%
failure_condition: Rank IC for the interaction signal and 20-day forward returns is greater than -0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 5.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to the contractionary impact of higher interest rates on corporate earnings growth and valuation multiples.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances during monetary tightening cycles, or the Rank IC is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 thousand units in the past month signals weak consumer demand and residential investment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns due to reduced economic activity and corporate revenue concerns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1200.0 in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where HOUST falls below 1200.0, or the Rank IC is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 104.0 in the past month indicates a weakening supply chain and economic slowdown, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns due to reduced corporate output and earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 104.0 in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances where INDPRO falls below 104.0, or the Rank IC is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) above 470000.0 million dollars in the past month signals strong economic growth and robust consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises above 470000.0 in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances where RSAFS rises above 470000.0, or the Rank IC is less than 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 5.0% over the past month signals immediate labor market weakness, which typically causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened recession fears and reduced consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 5.0% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances where UNRATE rises above 5.0% in the past month, or the Rank IC is less than 0.05.
